stem: An infant is diagnosed with ankyloglossia during an oral examination; what may be required for management?

options.text: Reassurance that it will always resolve without intervention

explanation: Frenectomy may be required for ankyloglossia. This is the management option directly associated with tongue-tie when restriction is clinically significant.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: Ankyloglossia can restrict tongue movement and may need frenectomy when intervention is indicated.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because ankyloglossia, or tongue-tie, may require frenectomy if it is causing functional problems.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because an eruption cyst is a bluish swelling over an erupting tooth, not tongue-tie.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a natal tooth is a tooth present at birth and may need extraction if it is loose or causing trauma.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because antibiotics are used for infection-related facial swelling, not as the primary management of ankyloglossia.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because ankyloglossia does not always resolve spontaneously and may need treatment if symptomatic.
